comments.original_comment:
Private investment and public funding of scientific research play fundamentally different and complementary roles. One cannot replace the other. Private capital follows a path to profit, investing in research where the commercial application is clearly visible. Thus, private capital is excellent at developing and scaling proven technologies. But it is poorly suited to fund the earliest, most speculative research, where the outcome is unknown and the breakthrough isn’t yet clear.

Public funding fills this gap. It takes the risks that private capital does not, and in doing so, creates the conditions that make private investment successful later. Almost all of the most exciting technological and medical advances securing billions in investment today, like AI, GLP-1s, semiconductor chips, 3D-printing, ohh, and rockets, and Internet, all started with basic research.

To continue all this world-changing and world-dominating research, we need to withdraw §200.340: so active and scientifically sound research studies could NOT be canceled willy nilly by flip-flopping “current priorities”.

Stephen Miller or Ross Vought's kids benefitted from publicly-funded cystic fibrosis research, and definitely vaccine research too. And now they don't want anyone else's kids to benefit from similarly stellar quality research. By the way, research for mRNA COVID vaccines was significantly funded by NIH. So we will have a grand old extinction event that only kill poor people the next time a virus spreads and makes Ebola look like kiddie pool. Viruses don't care about geopolitics and borders, but I guess the likes of RFK Jr. surely will be so winning and ensure America’s survival?

We need to withdraw §200.205: so political appointees cannot overrule highly qualified scientists to decide which research gets funded. Because America’s progress depends on it. Otherwise China is gonna take over as the next global superpower. They are beating (or will soon beat) America in robotics and any tech with rare-earth metals. They will most definitely not collaborate with America, but conquer everyone instead. Look at them trying to start pissing contests with long-range missiles. 

Forget about the golden days of the 1960's when American science was at its peak and beating Soviets. There was some good time with computers in the 80's and internet in the 2000's but that's never happening again with America, if science research becomes totally private and partisan politics. I thought what sets humanity apart from other creatures on Earth is the ability to seek evidence and learn from experiments and exploration, not just blindly follow the whims of the prevailing government or corporations.   

Politically and privately-motivated research will always benefit the shareholders at the expense of everyone else. Researchers need to access scientific literature and go to conferences to do their best work and maintain leadership of American science in the world. We need to withdraw §200.454 and §200.432, in addition to §200.205 and §200.340 as mentioned before. Thank you for your considerations.
